trust_decision.summary: The -b byte count from the sd_stress shell command line is used without validation as the malloc size. A failed or zero-size allocation is then written to by memset with no NULL check. The fix adds a 1-10000 range check where the option is parsed.

landing_point.why: The summary names sd_stress and a NULL dereference, so the unchecked malloc/memset pair is the first place anyone would look.

fix_sites.entry_point: usage text only (fix.diff:13-14), not a code site

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The malloc result is still unchecked after the fix. A solver could argue that with the size bounded to 10000 the allocation 'cannot fail', so the NULL check is unnecessary.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid byte counts 1-10000 (default 100) and the -r run count must keep working. An over-broad fix that rejects large or hex values (strtol base 0) would break legitimate use.

O6_input_shapes: -b negative (wraps to a huge unsigned value)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The malloc return is not NULL-checked before memset. Even in-range sizes can fail on low-RAM NuttX boards, so the NULL write is still possible.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The size is now bounded and small, so an allocation failure looks theoretical.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, two lines from the fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Remove the `if (block_alloc)` NULL check after the size-derived malloc in sd_bench.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the same SD test-utility family, with a user-sized buffer. The pattern is identical, but it is a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Drop the NULL check on the CLI-sized _write_data malloc.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CLI-controlled write size feeds malloc the same way. Again WHERE-type only.

O9_family: memory safety: NULL pointer dereference from unchecked allocation with an unvalidated CLI size (CWE-476)

O10_build.toolchain: PX4 CMake/Kconfig with arm-none-eabi GCC for NuttX boards; the posix/SITL build may compile the module, but SITL does not enable it by default
O10_build.project_tests: none for sd_stress; no unit tests in src/systemcmds/sd_stress/

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (!bytes) return -ENOMEM;` after malloc. This alone closes the NULL write and is arguably more complete than the published range check.

out_of_scope_notes: -r num_runs is also parsed with strtol and never validated (src/systemcmds/sd_stress/sd_stress.cpp:186). It only controls the loop count, so it has no memory-safety impact.
create_dir/remove_dir ignore their path argument and use TEMPDIR/TEMPDIR2 (src/systemcmds/sd_stress/sd_stress.cpp:69,81). This is a correctness bug, not a security issue.
